meta.title: HIPAA Security Rule crosswalk
meta.framework: 45 CFR Part 164, Subpart C (Security Rule), text in force August 2026
scope_notes: The mapping covers the Security Rule (Subpart C) only. It excludes the Privacy Rule (Subpart E) and the Breach Notification Rule (Subpart D). Breach response is operationally addressed by INC-01/INC-02 and COM-02, but those obligations are legal duties outside a controls mapping and are deliberately not rows here.

The SOC 2 opinion covers the Trust Services Criteria only. This crosswalk feeds Section 5 of the report (Other Information, unaudited, no opinion expressed) and the prep-phase HIPAA coverage view. It is never a compliance certification.

Verification sources: 45 CFR 164.308, 164.310, 164.312, 164.314, 164.316 via Cornell LII (current text), checked 2026-08-04. The January 2025 NPRM that would eliminate the addressable category is still proposed; HHS moved it to long-term actions with final action anticipated July 2027. This mapping targets the rule in force.
Row convention: every standard and every implementation specification is a row. Standards whose substance lives in their specifications resolve as roll-ups of the child rows.

resolutions.covered: Fully carried by mapped controls already in the library
resolutions.covered_attr: Carried by an existing control that gains one HIPAA-gated attribute so the ePHI delta is tested, not just advised
resolutions.covered_note: Carried by mapped controls, with a HIPAA lens note that becomes prep guidance
resolutions.inherited: Carried partly by the cloud provider's controls, monitored through VND-02, plus entity-level controls where facilities exist
resolutions.new_control: Requires one of the three drafted HIP controls
resolutions.rollup: Standard met through its implementation specifications (child rows)
resolutions.na: Not applicable to the client population this add-on serves

rows.name: Security management process
rows.rationale: Met through the four specifications below; the umbrella process is the risk assessment cycle (RSK-01), risk-based control design (RSK-02), deficiency remediation (EVL-02) and the approved policy suite (POL-01).

rows.name: Risk analysis
rows.rationale: RSK-01 A1 to A7 require a formal assessment of threats, vulnerabilities, likelihood and impact within the last 12 months; AST-01 A4 documents data flows.
rows.note: Gated attribute on RSK-01 tests that the risk analysis explicitly identifies where ePHI is created, received, maintained and transmitted.

rows.name: Risk management
rows.rationale: RSK-02 A1/A2 map each significant risk to at least one control; EVL-02 A3/A4 track corrective action plans to completion.

rows.name: Sanction policy
rows.rationale: GOV-01 A2 documents a disciplinary process for violations; PPL-04 A2 defines consequences for policy violations and A4 evidences corrective action taken.
rows.note: Gated attribute on GOV-01 tests that the disciplinary process explicitly reaches violations of security policies and procedures.

rows.name: Information system activity review
rows.rationale: MON-01 collects and retains security event logs; MON-02 A3 evidences triage of alerts within defined timeframes; IAM-05 reviews access reports periodically.

rows.name: Assigned security responsibility
rows.rationale: GOV-03 A2 formally assigns security and compliance responsibilities; GOV-04 A1 identifies an oversight recipient independent of day to day engineering.
rows.note: Gated attribute on GOV-03 tests that a security official is designated by name, not only by function.

rows.name: Workforce security
rows.rationale: Met through the three specifications below.

rows.name: Authorization and/or supervision
rows.rationale: IAM-03 A2/A4 require documented authorization by an authorized approver before access; IAM-06 assigns access by role.

rows.name: Workforce clearance procedure
rows.rationale: PPL-01 A1 to A5 require background checks for all personnel including contractors prior to or at start, with completion tested for each person.

rows.name: Termination procedures
rows.rationale: IAM-04 A1 to A5: documented offboarding, defined maximum removal timeframe, per-termination evidence that all in-scope access was removed on time.

rows.name: Information access management
rows.rationale: Met through the specifications below.

rows.name: Isolating health care clearinghouse functions
rows.rationale: Applies only when the organization contains a health care clearinghouse inside a larger organization. Not the client population this add-on serves; the scoping profile should confirm and record this.
rows.note: If a future client is or contains a clearinghouse, this row becomes a scoping question, not a control.

rows.name: Access authorization
rows.rationale: IAM-03 A1/A2 document the provisioning process with authorization before grant; IAM-06 A1/A2 define roles and assign access through them.

rows.name: Access establishment and modification
rows.rationale: IAM-03 A5 verifies granted access matches the authorized request; IAM-04 adjusts access on role changes; IAM-05 A3 to A6 review and remediate periodically.

rows.name: Security awareness and training
rows.rationale: PPL-03 A1/A2/A4: curriculum exists, timing defined for onboarding and ongoing completion, completion tested for each person within the defined period.

rows.name: Security reminders
rows.rationale: PPL-03 A2/A4 require periodic recurring training; POL-02 A4 communicates policy and system changes to affected personnel.

rows.name: Protection from malicious software
rows.rationale: END-01 A1/A4/A5 deploy anti-malware protection with automatic updates and evidence threats are remediated.
rows.note: Prep guidance: the training curriculum should include malware and phishing awareness (PPL-03 A1 topic list).

rows.name: Log-in monitoring
rows.rationale: MON-01 A2 includes authentication events in required log categories; MON-02 A1 alerts on key threat scenarios including anomalous sign-in activity.

rows.name: Password management
rows.rationale: IAM-01 A3 tiers authentication strength by system sensitivity; IAM-02 enforces MFA on all in-scope systems.
rows.note: Addressable spec: SSO and passwordless or MFA-first authentication satisfies it as a stronger equivalent; document that choice in the access control policy.

rows.name: Security incident procedures
rows.rationale: INC-01 A1 to A3: documented IR plan covering roles, severity, containment through recovery and communication, reviewed within 12 months.

rows.name: Response and reporting
rows.rationale: INC-02 A2 to A7 evidence containment, root cause, restoration, notification and documentation for each incident; MON-02 A4 defines escalation into incident response.

rows.name: Contingency plan
rows.rationale: BCP-01 A1 to A3: documented BCP/DR plan with critical systems, recovery objectives, procedures and responsible personnel. BCP-01 carries CC9.1, so it is in scope for every engagement including Security-only.

rows.name: Data backup plan
rows.rationale: BCP-02 A1 to A4: automated backups of critical data on schedule, monitored, stored in a geographically separate location; A6 evidences successful restoration tests (retrievable exact copies).

rows.name: Disaster recovery plan
rows.rationale: BCP-01 A3 documents recovery procedures with responsible personnel; BCP-02 A5/A6 provide alternate processing capability and tested restoration.

rows.name: Emergency mode operation plan
rows.rationale: BCP-01 A2/A3 identify critical systems and continuity procedures; BCP-02 A5 provides failover infrastructure.
rows.note: Gated attribute on BCP-01 tests that the plan states how ePHI security protections continue during emergency mode operations, not only how service is restored.

rows.name: Testing and revision procedures
rows.rationale: BCP-01 A5/A6: plan tested within the last 12 months with documented results, and updated based on findings.

rows.name: Applications and data criticality analysis
rows.rationale: BCP-01 A2 identifies critical systems with recovery time and recovery point objectives, which is the criticality ranking this spec asks for.

rows.name: Evaluation
rows.rationale: EVL-01 A2/A3: management security posture review plus an independent evaluation within the last year (the SOC 2 examination itself qualifies); RSK-01 A11/A12 update the assessment on significant change.

rows.name: Business associate contracts and other arrangements
rows.rationale: VND-01 A5/A8/A9 put security, confidentiality and data processing terms in vendor contracts, but a business associate agreement is a specific statutory contract with mandated clauses. HIP-01 requires identification of every ePHI counterparty and a signed BAA both upstream and downstream.

rows.name: Written contract or other arrangement
rows.rationale: HIP-01 A2/A3 verify signed BAAs for customer relationships and subcontractors that handle ePHI.

rows.name: Facility access controls
rows.rationale: Met through the four specifications below. For cloud infrastructure the data center layer is the provider's controls, monitored through VND-02; NET-03 covers any entity facilities and is N/A-eligible for fully remote companies.

rows.name: Contingency operations (facility access)
rows.rationale: Facility access in support of data restoration is a data center function inherited from the cloud provider (VND-02 A2/A4 review its SOC 2 report); BCP-01 documents entity-side recovery responsibilities.

rows.name: Facility security plan
rows.rationale: NET-03 A1/A2 restrict facility and sensitive area access where the entity has premises; data center safeguarding is provider-inherited via VND-02.

rows.name: Access control and validation procedures
rows.rationale: NET-03 A1/A4 authorize access by role and log visitors where premises exist; provider-inherited at the data center layer.

rows.name: Maintenance records
rows.rationale: Records of repairs to physical security components are a facility operator function, provider-inherited for cloud and landlord-managed offices; NET-03 A5 gives the periodic entity-side review where applicable. Addressable, so the documented rationale is the compliance artifact.

rows.name: Workstation use
rows.rationale: POL-01 A1 requires an acceptable use policy specifying proper workstation functions; END-02 A3 governs removable media usage.

rows.name: Workstation security
rows.rationale: END-01 A1 to A4: endpoint protection deployed with enforced disk encryption, screen lock and automatic updates on all managed endpoints.

rows.name: Device and media controls
rows.rationale: Met through the four specifications below.

rows.name: Disposal
rows.rationale: DAT-02 A1 to A3: disposal procedure with wiping and destruction methods, evidence of wipe before each disposal, documented with date, method and asset identification.

rows.name: Media re-use
rows.rationale: DAT-02 A1/A2 cover removal of data before assets are returned or repurposed, including cloud storage destruction per provider procedures.

rows.name: Accountability (media movement)
rows.rationale: AST-01 A1 to A3 maintain an asset inventory including endpoints with designated owners, reviewed periodically.
rows.note: Served with the row below by the gated attribute on DAT-03 (policy position on local ePHI storage), alongside the AST-01 endpoint inventory.

rows.name: Data backup and storage (before movement)
rows.rationale: BCP-02 A1/A4 maintain retrievable copies independent of any single device; DAT-03 A3 protects removable media and endpoints.
rows.note: Gated attribute on DAT-03 tests that policy addresses local ePHI storage on endpoints and removable media (prohibited, or inventoried and protected). Also serves the accountability row above.

rows.name: Access control
rows.rationale: Met through the four specifications below plus role-based least privilege (IAM-06) and privileged access management (IAM-07).

rows.name: Unique user identification
rows.rationale: IAM-01 A1: all users uniquely identified, no shared accounts for interactive use.

rows.name: Emergency access procedure
rows.rationale: IAM-07 governs standing privileged access but nothing in the library covers break-glass access to ePHI when normal access paths are unavailable. HIP-02 documents the procedure, restricts and secures the emergency path, and reviews any use.

rows.name: Automatic logoff
rows.rationale: END-01 A3 enforces screen lock on managed endpoints; IAM-01 A3 tiers authentication strength by sensitivity.
rows.note: Addressable: enforced screen lock plus SSO session policies is the accepted equivalent; where the product admin plane supports idle session timeout, prep guidance recommends enabling it.

rows.name: Encryption and decryption (at rest)
rows.rationale: DAT-01 A1/A3/A4/A5: encryption at rest on all in-scope systems with current algorithms and managed keys.

rows.name: Audit controls
rows.rationale: MON-01 A1 to A4 record and retain authentication, access, configuration and admin activity with tamper protection; IAM-07 A3 logs privileged activity.

rows.name: Integrity
rows.rationale: Improper alteration or destruction is constrained by access controls, encryption (DAT-01), logged change activity (MON-01) and retrievable exact copies with tested restores (BCP-02 A6).
rows.note: Addressable mechanism below; the standard is met by the combination, documented in the mapped policy.

rows.name: Mechanism to authenticate ePHI
rows.rationale: TLS integrity protection in transit (DAT-01 A2/A3), managed-database checksumming at rest and successful restoration tests (BCP-02 A6) corroborate that ePHI has not been altered or destroyed in an unauthorized manner.
rows.note: Addressable: document these mechanisms as the corroboration measure in the data protection policy.

rows.name: Person or entity authentication
rows.rationale: IAM-01 A2 requires authentication before access; IAM-02 enforces MFA across in-scope systems with enrollment verified across users.

rows.name: Transmission security
rows.rationale: DAT-01 A2: TLS 1.2 or higher for all in-scope connections.

rows.name: Integrity controls (transmission)
rows.rationale: TLS provides in-transit integrity protection against undetected modification (DAT-01 A2/A3).

rows.name: Encryption (transmission)
rows.rationale: DAT-01 A2 encrypts data in transit for all in-scope connections.

rows.name: Business associate contracts or other arrangements (content)
rows.rationale: HIP-01 A4 verifies BAA terms carry the content this standard mandates.

rows.name: Business associate contract content
rows.rationale: HIP-01 A4: BAA includes Security Rule compliance, subcontractor flow-down per 164.308(b)(2), and security incident reporting including breaches.

rows.name: Other arrangements
rows.rationale: Applies when covered entity and business associate are both government entities using a memorandum of understanding instead of a contract. Not the client population this add-on serves.
rows.note: If a client contracts directly with a government covered entity under an MOU, treat this row as in scope through HIP-01 with the MOU as the instrument.

rows.name: Business associate contracts with subcontractors
rows.rationale: HIP-01 A3 verifies signed downstream BAAs for every subcontractor that handles ePHI.

rows.name: Requirements for group health plans
rows.rationale: Applies to group health plans and their plan sponsors. SaaS business associates are not group health plans; the scoping profile records this.

rows.name: Policies and procedures
rows.rationale: POL-01 A1 to A6: approved policy suite across the required security domains with named owners, periodic review and operational procedures.

rows.name: Documentation
rows.rationale: Policies are maintained in written electronic form (POL-02 A2 accessible storage) with operational procedures documented (POL-01 A3).
rows.note: Records of required actions and assessments (risk analyses, reviews, incident records) exist as the evidence corpus each control produces; HIP-03 adds the retention requirement below.

rows.name: Time limit (6 year retention)
rows.rationale: No existing control sets a retention floor for security documentation. DAT-03 governs customer data retention, which is a different object. HIP-03 requires six year retention of security policies and activity records from creation or last effective date.

rows.name: Availability (of documentation)
rows.rationale: POL-02 A2/A3: policies stored somewhere accessible and training points personnel to where relevant policies live.

rows.name: Updates (to documentation)
rows.rationale: POL-01 A5 reviews and approves policies on a defined cadence; RSK-01 A11 updates the risk assessment when significant changes occur.

gated_attributes.text: Risk assessment identifies the systems and data flows where ePHI is created, received, maintained, or transmitted
gated_attributes.typical_evidence: The risk assessment document, with an ePHI scope section or ePHI-flagged rows in the asset and flow inventory
gated_attributes.pass_criteria: PASS: The risk assessment names the specific systems and data flows handling ePHI, consistent with the asset inventory (AST-01). FAIL: The assessment is generic with no identification of where ePHI lives, or contradicts the asset inventory.

gated_attributes.text: The disciplinary process explicitly covers failures to comply with security policies and procedures, including those protecting ePHI
gated_attributes.typical_evidence: The disciplinary or sanctions section of the Code of Conduct or security policy
gated_attributes.pass_criteria: PASS: Documented consequences expressly apply to failures to comply with security policies and procedures, and the language reaches policies protecting ePHI (naming ePHI, HIPAA, or the security policy suite that governs it). FAIL: Discipline is documented only for general conduct, or the sanctions language cannot be read to reach security policy violations.

gated_attributes.text: A security official is designated by name as responsible for developing and implementing the policies and procedures that protect ePHI (the HIPAA Security Officer role)
gated_attributes.typical_evidence: Policy suite ownership page, org chart annotation, or a designation memo naming the individual
gated_attributes.pass_criteria: PASS: A specific named individual is designated as responsible for the security program covering ePHI (a HIPAA Security Officer designation, or an equivalent named assignment). FAIL: Responsibility is assigned to a function or team with no identifiable individual, or the designation exists but cannot be tied to ePHI protection.

gated_attributes.text: The contingency plan addresses how security protections for ePHI continue during emergency mode operations
gated_attributes.typical_evidence: Emergency mode or degraded operations section of the BCP/DR plan
gated_attributes.pass_criteria: PASS: The plan states how access control, logging, and data protection are maintained (or consciously constrained with compensating steps) while operating in emergency mode. FAIL: The plan covers only restoration of service with nothing on protecting ePHI during degraded operations.

gated_attributes.text: Policy addresses local storage of ePHI on endpoints and removable media
gated_attributes.typical_evidence: Data handling or acceptable use policy section on local storage of ePHI
gated_attributes.pass_criteria: PASS: Policy either prohibits storing ePHI on endpoints and removable media, or requires that any such storage is inventoried, encrypted, and backed up before device movement. FAIL: No policy position on local ePHI storage.

new_controls.title: Business Associate Agreements
new_controls.na_trigger: Is the HIPAA compliance add-on in scope for this engagement?
new_controls.description: {company_name} executes business associate agreements before electronic protected health information is created, received, maintained, or transmitted on its behalf or on behalf of a customer, and with every subcontractor that handles ePHI. Agreements include the content required by 45 CFR 164.314(a), including security incident reporting and subcontractor flow-down.

attributes.text: Counterparties that create, receive, maintain, or transmit ePHI are identified
attributes.typical_evidence: Vendor or customer inventory with an ePHI flag, or a data flow document naming ePHI counterparties
attributes.pass_criteria: PASS: An inventory or data flow document identifies which customers and subcontractors handle ePHI, and it is consistent with the vendor inventory in VND-01. FAIL: No identification of ePHI-handling counterparties, or the list contradicts the vendor inventory.

attributes.text: For each customer relationship involving ePHI: a signed BAA is in place
attributes.typical_evidence: Executed BAA documents with signature dates
attributes.pass_criteria: PASS: Each ePHI customer relationship has a BAA signed on or before the date ePHI handling began. FAIL: Any relationship lacks a signed BAA, or the BAA postdates the start of ePHI handling with no documented interim arrangement.

attributes.text: For each subcontractor that handles ePHI: a signed downstream BAA is in place
attributes.typical_evidence: Executed subcontractor BAAs, including cloud provider BAA (for example the AWS, GCP, or Azure BAA)
attributes.pass_criteria: PASS: Each ePHI-handling subcontractor, including the cloud infrastructure provider, has a signed BAA. FAIL: Any ePHI-handling subcontractor operates without a BAA. Note: a subcontractor that only transmits ePHI transiently and never stores it, or a service that receives no ePHI at all, may be excluded only with a documented rationale. A vendor that stores or maintains ePHI remains a business associate even when the data is encrypted and the vendor holds no decryption key.

attributes.text: BAA terms include the elements required by 45 CFR 164.314(a)(2)
attributes.typical_evidence: The BAA template or executed agreements
attributes.pass_criteria: PASS: Terms require Security Rule compliance, flow-down of the same obligations to subcontractors, and upstream reporting of security incidents including breaches. FAIL: Any of the three required elements is absent from the operative BAA.

new_controls.title: Emergency Access Procedure
new_controls.na_trigger: Is the HIPAA compliance add-on in scope for this engagement?
new_controls.description: {company_name} maintains a documented emergency access procedure for obtaining access to systems containing electronic protected health information when normal access paths are unavailable. Emergency credentials are restricted and secured, and any use is logged and reviewed afterward.

attributes.text: Emergency access procedure is documented, covering when it applies and who may invoke it
attributes.typical_evidence: Break-glass or emergency access section of the access control policy or runbook
attributes.pass_criteria: PASS: A documented procedure defines the circumstances that qualify as an emergency, who is authorized to invoke emergency access, and the steps to obtain it. FAIL: No documented emergency access procedure, or the procedure names no authorized personnel.

attributes.text: Emergency access paths are inventoried, restricted, and secured
attributes.typical_evidence: Break-glass account list, vault entry, or root credential storage configuration
attributes.pass_criteria: PASS: Emergency credentials or access paths are enumerated, limited to the personnel named in the procedure, and stored securely (vault, sealed credential, or hardware token). FAIL: Emergency credentials are undocumented, broadly available, or stored in plaintext.

attributes.text: For each emergency access use (if any): use was logged and reviewed afterward
attributes.typical_evidence: Access logs for the break-glass identity plus the post-use review record
attributes.pass_criteria: PASS: Each use is logged and has a documented after-the-fact review confirming the use was appropriate. FAIL: Any use is unlogged or lacks a post-use review. If no uses occurred in the period, the attribute passes on the logging configuration being in place.

new_controls.title: Security Documentation Retention
new_controls.na_trigger: Is the HIPAA compliance add-on in scope for this engagement?
new_controls.description: {company_name} retains its security policies and the records of required security activities, including risk assessments, access reviews, incident documentation, and training records, for at least six years from creation or the date last in effect, whichever is later, and can retrieve historical versions.

attributes.text: A six year retention requirement is defined for security policies and security activity records
attributes.typical_evidence: Retention schedule or policy governance section naming the six year floor for security documentation
attributes.pass_criteria: PASS: A documented retention requirement of at least six years covers security policies and the records of security activities (risk assessments, reviews, incidents, training). FAIL: No retention requirement for security documentation, or a period shorter than six years.

attributes.text: Historical versions of policies and security records are retrievable
attributes.typical_evidence: Document repository version history, archive folder, or system-of-record retention configuration
attributes.pass_criteria: PASS: The storage system demonstrably preserves prior versions (version history enabled, archive maintained, or deletion restricted) so a document from an earlier period can be produced. FAIL: Prior versions are overwritten or deleted with no archive.
